Definition: adverb from G2986; brilliantly, i.e. figuratively, luxuriously:--sumptuously.
BiblicalUsage: Sumptuously is the adverb for living in luxury, and it appears once, in the parable of the rich man in Luke 16:19: he "was clothed in purple and fine linen, and fared sumptuously every day."
TheologicalSignificance: My position is that the one adverb carries the whole parable: he fared sumptuously every day, and Lazarus lay at his gate, and the luxury is the indictment.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
